A1.justification: Both 25-page PDFs describe the same TerraMind work. Their complete main text, equations, tables, figures and supplementary material support reliable comparison, including matching the renumbered appendix sections.

before.justification: v4 reports original TerraMind generation, classification, segmentation, tokenizer and Thinking-in-Modalities experiments in Section 5 and the supplementary material.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark scores, tokenizer evaluations and supplementary generation examples.

M1.justification: The tokenizers, dual-scale encoder-decoder architecture, masked-token objective, generation procedure and Thinking-in-Modalities recursion are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same TerraMesh training coverage, nine PANGAEA tasks, EuroSAT and METER-ML classification, South Africa crop mapping and generation scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the corresponding experiments, including CLIP, DeCUR, Prithvi, U-Net/ViT and Dynamic World comparisons. The added JUWELS citation is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Training configurations, the frozen-encoder PANGAEA protocol, few-shot sampling and testing procedures, and generation evaluations using 10 diffusion steps are retained without revision.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same fusion and modality ablations, FSQ-versus-VQ analyses, codebook and EMA investigations, geographic error analyses, pseudo-label comparisons and TiM experiments.

E5.justification: Tables 5 and 11 retain mean accuracy averaged over 200 runs. Monte Carlo sampling descriptions and uncertainty-reporting practices are also unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout. For example, Table 6 retains average mIoU values of 58.35 and 59.57 for TerraMindv1-B and TerraMindv1-L; supplementary results and generation images are unchanged.

T1.justification: The cross-entropy objective, random-model loss calculation and TiM equations retain identical mathematical content. No definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about any-to-any generation, dual-scale learning, TiM, embedding quality and benchmark performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations remain unchanged, including tokenizer detail loss, radar reconstruction difficulties, geolocation confusion and inaccurate generations from inputs with limited information.

D1.justification: New Section 7 identifies JUWELS at Jülich Supercomputing Centre and computing support from the Gauss Centre. Existing GPU specifications, training times, hyperparameters and code/data disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: v5 adds Alvarez's 2021 JUWELS facility paper as reference 3 in the acknowledgements. All 76 existing references are retained, and the related-work discussion and research positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: v5 inserts an acknowledgements section between the conclusion and references. Supplementary Sections 7–11 become Sections 8–12, while the scientific prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgement and reference additions reflow the bibliography, while appendix heading renumbering causes small shifts in text and figure placement. Figure designs, plotted content and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v5 adds ESA FAST-EO funding and JUWELS computing-support attribution. This modest disclosure update leaves the scientific explanations, experimental evidence, implementation settings and limitations unchanged; the accompanying reflow has no material effect on overall quality.
